obligation: HIPAA Security Rule
basis: A health care provider that transmits health information electronically in standard transactions is a covered entity (45 CFR 160.103); the group's payer and clearinghouse agreements cover electronic claims, eligibility and remittance, and it is organized as a single covered entity. It is also a business associate for the 45 SL-1 client practices. No size exemption; 164.306(b) affects how, not whether. Not applicable within the rule: 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(A), because the group performs no clearinghouse function; 164.314(a)(2)(ii), because there are no arrangements between governmental entities; and 164.314(b), because the employee health plan is a separate covered entity. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: HIPAA Privacy Rule
basis: Same covered entity and business associate status; only safeguard-related provisions are analyzed in these deliverables. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
basis: Covered entity (164.404-164.408) and business associate for SL-1 clients (164.410). Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM (2025)
basis: Not a final rule; counsel's memo lists it as pending. Tracked for planning

obligation: 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD records)
basis: The group runs no federally assisted substance use disorder program, but it receives Part 2 records from outside programs with patient consent, so it is a lawful holder: 2.16(a) security policies apply; 2.16(b) does not. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
basis: 16 CFR 318.1 excludes HIPAA covered entities and business associates acting as such; the patient-app platform runs under HIPAA for the group's own patients and under BAAs for client practices. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Section 1557: patient care decision support tools
basis: The group receives federal financial assistance (Medicare, Medicaid in 4 states) and operates a health program; its AI portfolio includes clinical decision support tools

obligation: CMS Emergency Preparedness conditions
citation: 42 CFR 482.15 and parallel rules; 42 CFR 416.54 for ASCs
basis: The 6 ASCs are Medicare-certified ambulatory surgical centers, so 42 CFR 416.54 applies to them. The clinics, imaging centers and lab are not provider types covered by the emergency preparedness rules and follow the enterprise contingency program

obligation: HIPAA applicability to social assistance
basis: The group is a medical group and provides no social assistance services

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: CLIA test report and record retention
basis: The central lab holds a CLIA certificate; only the LIS-dependent test report and retention provisions are analyzed

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over ERP and payroll are tested by the SOX program and not repeated here

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification; worked example)
basis: The group holds personal information of Florida residents at its Florida sites. Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Breach notification and data security laws of other states
citation: Statutes of Georgia, Alabama, South Carolina and each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Sites in 4 states and patients who reside elsewhere; notify under the law of each state of residence, using counsel's state matrix

obligation: Recording consent (worked example)
basis: The AI scribe records visits; the group applies all-party prior consent in all four states, with Florida as the worked example. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer approval before any ransom payment

obligation: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act
basis: Final rule not published at intake; counsel's memo lists it as pending; reporting is voluntary until it takes effect. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: Federal contract clauses on covered telecommunications and Kaspersky products
basis: No federal contracts in the contract repository; recheck if one is signed

obligation: Client agreements for SL-1 and SL-2 (assurance reports, notice and availability terms)
basis: SL-1 clients receive an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report and 10-day breach notice under their BAAs; SL-2 client agreements set interface, security and turnaround terms, and the health system clients ask for a SOC 2 report
